A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cumulative Reasoning work. All 21 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v5, including appendices, are readable, and their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Tables 1–4 report original CR evaluations on FOLIO-wiki, curated FOLIO-wiki, AutoTNLI, and Game of 24.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, with additional MATH evaluations and FOLIO component ablations in Tables 5–8 and 13. Tables 9–12 are separately attributed to third-party reproductions.

M1.justification: The core proposer–verifier–reporter framework remains. However, Section 5.2 and Figure 7 introduce an implemented Python-assisted variant using a single reasoning context, with answer sketches, code execution, observations, and subsequent answers. This substantially extends inference and verification beyond v1's implementation through differently prompted LLM roles.

E1.justification: v5 adds MATH evaluation spanning seven mathematical subjects and five difficulty levels, substantially extending the earlier logic and arithmetic-puzzle coverage. Appendix A.1 also adds LogiQA, ProofWriter, and LogicalDeduction comparisons explicitly drawn from third-party reproductions. The original benchmark coverage remains.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in the original Tables 1–4 remain unchanged. New MATH comparisons introduce Complex CoT with and without Progressive-Hint Prompting, plus PAL and ToRA for Python-assisted reasoning, including reproduced baseline results in Tables 5–8.

E3.justification: New MATH protocols specify a 500-problem subset, greedy decoding, 4-shot CR versus 8-shot Complex CoT, and Python experiments defaulting to GPT-4-turbo with 2-shot CR versus 4-shot PAL/ToRA. Game of 24 expands tested branch counts from 1–2 to 1–5 while retaining 100 games and the 50-iteration limit. These are added protocols rather than revisions to the retained logic experiments.

E4.justification: New Table 13 ablates the verifier, random premise selection, and both together on FOLIO-wiki using GPT-3.5-turbo; v1 contains no equivalent component ablations. v5 also expands the Game of 24 branch-count sweep and adds PHP comparisons and a worked MATH case. The earlier FOLIO and FraCas examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. CoT-SC sampling counts and PHP iteration counts describe inference procedures, while the Game of 24 state-count bounds concern computational effort rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: FOLIO and AutoTNLI accuracies remain unchanged. Game of 24 retains 84%/94% at branches 1/2, replaces provisional state-count bounds of 50.00/51.04 with reported counts of 11.68/13.70, and adds branches 3–5 with 97%, 97%, and 98% accuracy. New MATH configurations report 58.0% with PHP without code and 72.2% with Python. Extensive ablation and third-party result rows are added; Table 11 reports CR at 69.11% versus ToT at 69.12% on FOLIO-val.

T1.justification: New Appendix B defines arrival probabilities, introduces perfect-verifier, unique-path, and monotonic-context assumptions, and supplies Lemma B.3 and Theorem B.4 with proofs comparing CoT-SC, ToT, and CR. v1 has no equivalent formal analysis. v5 also corrects the Boolean identity from 1 ∧ x = 1 to 1 ∧ x = x.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion expand the contributions to MATH performance and Python-assisted reasoning. The headline Game of 24 claim changes from 94% accuracy and a 20-point advantage to 98% and 24 points, supported by the newly tested wider configuration. The original CR proposal and logical-inference claims remain.

C2.justification: v5 adds substantive arguments about FOL expressiveness, translation misalignment, undecidability, and the difficulty of constructing HOL programs, beyond v1's dataset-error discussion. It adds interpretations of Python feedback as verification and mathematical performance as evidence of broader applicability. Section 5 also discusses context-length constraints and possible training overlap motivating the MATH subset.

D1.justification: v5 adds a work-specific code-access link and an explicit CR-with-code meta-prompt template in Figure 7. It documents MATH prompting counts, model choices, decoding temperature, the 8k context constraint, and the single-session Python configuration. These provide substantial new reproducibility information beyond v1's general prompting and guidance-library details.

R1.justification: Research positioning expands to mathematical prompting and tool-assisted reasoning through Complex CoT, PHP, PAL, ToRA, Program of Thoughts, and Decomposed Prompting. New formal-logic and Self-Refine/Reflexion references support additional arguments. The System 1/System 2 citation also changes from Goel et al. to Kahneman.

P1.justification: Most pre-existing prose and the main section sequence remain recognizable. Changes include localized wording corrections, merging the logic preliminaries, and moving detailed HOL exposition into Appendix C; the earlier dataset appendix becomes Appendix D. Much of the additional writing accompanies new scientific content rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v5 substantially reorganizes the displays: Tables 1 and 2 appear side by side, Tables 1–3 omit error-rate columns, and existing diagrams are redrawn or restyled. It adds MATH, supplementary-comparison, and ablation tables, along with mathematical examples, the code meta-prompt, and the CoT-SC/ToT/CR comparison diagram. The retained Hadid example becomes captioned Figure 4.

improvement.justification: The new MATH comparisons and Table 13 component ablations substantially strengthen evidence for CR's applicability and the value of its components, which v1 did not directly test this way. The prompt template, code-access information, and replacement of provisional state-count bounds improve transparency. Appendix B remains conditional on strong assumptions, and experimental uncertainty is still unreported, but the gains in empirical support and reproducibility are substantial.
